Paragraph: "In this spring season, life without my lady is indeed impossible for me to live; see Lakshmana, how these peahens are dancing alongside their husbands..."
Situation/Problem_Faced: Rama expresses an inability to sustain life without Seetha during a season filled with romantic union.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama openly voices his deepest emotional reliance on Seetha to his brother.
Outcome/Resolution: He reaches a peak of emotional vulnerability, laying bare his despair.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Feelings of Hopelessness: Existential Despair, Suicidal Ideation / Inability to Live

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Praana-Samsaya (A state where life force itself feels threatened by intense sorrow and separation)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Reflects the absolute non-duality of love: the Divine cannot find fulfillment without His Shakti (Seetha), illustrating total spiritual interdependence.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Acute existential despair where loss of a core attachment figure makes continued survival feel impossible, amplified by seasonal emotional triggers.
